title: MAFIA: Multi-Adapter Fused Inclusive LanguAge Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotypical biases related to religion using intrinsic tests (StereoSet, CrowS-Pairs) and extrinsic tests. An extrinsic test, Bias-STS-B, was created to evaluate how religious terms affect semantic textual similarity scores. Additionally, the Jigsaw toxicity classification benchmark was used to measure unintended bias against religious identity groups in toxicity detection.
base_benchmarks: Jigsaw Unintended Bias in Toxicity Classification
findings: The proposed model, MAFIA, which fuses multiple debiasing adapters, successfully reduces religious bias on both intrinsic (StereoSet, CrowS-Pairs) and extrinsic (Bias-STS-B, Jigsaw toxicity classification) evaluations. It demonstrated improved fairness scores for religious dimensions compared to baseline models and single-debiasing methods, while also maintaining or improving overall task performance.
